title: Tokenizing 3D Molecule Structure with Quantized Spherical Coordinates

problem.claim: Direct application of language models to 3D molecular structure design is constrained by challenges in representing and generating 3D structures.

gap.claim: Existing approaches lack a 3D line notation that is SE(3)-invariant and supports autoregressive generation, while continuous spatial coordinates are incompatible with the discrete token inputs required by language models.

contributions.claim: Mol-StrucTok provides a unified framework for tokenizing 3D molecular structures.
Spherical Coordinate Notation encodes local atomic environments in spherical coordinates and is agnostic to 2D notations and inherently SE(3)-invariant.
A structure-aware VQ-VAE discretizes the spherical coordinates into chemically valid tokens suitable for language model processing.

author_reported_evidence.claim: In unconditional generation, Mol-StrucTok achieves diffusion-level stability with approximately 28× faster inference.
In conditional generation, Mol-StrucTok reduces property-matching MAE by 5–8× compared with diffusion-based methods.
The authors report that code is available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Language models have shown general-purpose capabilities, including molecule generation with SMILES and SELFIES, but their direct use for 3D structure design remains constrained.
The constraints involve designing an invariant autoregressive 3D notation and reconciling continuous coordinates with discrete language-model tokens.
Mol-StrucTok addresses the gap with spherical-coordinate notation, structure-aware vector quantization, and a GPT-2-style model for end-to-end 3D molecular generation.
The authors report task-dependent performance gains in unconditional stability and inference speed, and in conditional property matching.

source_observation.claim: Combining an invariant structural representation with discrete chemically valid tokens enables language-model-based processing of 3D molecular structures.

interpretation.claim: Representation design and discretization jointly address geometric invariance and language-model input constraints.

application.claim: For other continuous structured domains, consider invariant representations paired with domain-valid tokenization before applying autoregressive language models.

exception.claim: The reported advantages are task-dependent rather than uniformly established across all generation settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, evaluation protocols, or the definition of diffusion-level stability.
The abstract does not report molecular coverage, validity details, hardware, or inference-time measurement conditions.
The abstract does not provide ablations, failure cases, or limitations.
